source_review.notes: Reviewed current official LLVM TSan, ASan, UBSan, LSan, MSan and suppression documentation; GCC instrumentation; current NVIDIA Compute Sanitizer; and primary ASan/TSan papers. Tool scope, platform, overhead, compatibility, runtime security and device shared-memory limitations are retained.

evidence: Instrumented/uninstrumented code, configuration, execution, detection model, happens-before, matrix counts, suppressions and reports are distinct.
Observed cleanliness, coverage, limitation, false negative and false positive terminology is precise.
Recomputed 3*4*5*2=120, executed 113 and fraction 113/120=.9416667.
Recomputed Exercise 1 intended 1200, startable 1194, target-executed 1182 and completed 1164.
Snippet passed exact stdout and zero exit code.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts do not claim schedule/path completeness.

evidence: Verified clean claim is conditional on I,C,E,D and cannot universalize.
Checked intended/start/target/completed/report-free ledger implications.
Verified semantic fix must add ownership/HB/lifetime rule rather than timing.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No probability of race freedom is inferred.

evidence: Reviewed partial instrumentation, incompatible tools, missing symbols, setup abort, target timeout, optimizer/timing perturbation, cascade and suppression drift.
Reviewed host/device/MPI/foreign boundaries, GPU address-space limits, allocators/UAF/ABA, shutdown and production differences.
Reviewed report leakage/exhaustion, autonomous braking and clinical lab processing.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Covers build, dynamic coverage, memory models, runtimes, devices, CI, security and high-stakes use.

evidence: Build/link/runtime and all supported modules are audited and symbolizable.
Every matrix case has target/completion/report status; first report and raw evidence are preserved.
Fix obeys memory/lifetime model, regressions pass, suppressions remain narrow/owned, and blind spots remain explicit.
invariant_checking.notes: Checked evidence chain from build through release closure.

evidence: Race triage reconstructs object generation, conflicting accesses and missing happens-before.
Timing, volatile, disappearance and suppression are correctly rejected as proof.
Closure combines before/after reproducer, dynamic matrix, systematic/functional and optimized evidence with limitations.
proof_review.notes: No clean run is treated as universal safety proof.

evidence: Tool guarantees, observed reports, coverage claims, semantic proof and production evidence are separate.
Snippet disclaims sanitizer execution, schedule enumeration and correctness.
Braking/lab cases name reviewers and claim none.
Matrix arithmetic reproduced exactly.
Required evidence includes exact builds/options, instrumented modules, seeds/schedules/topology, raw/symbolized reports, target status, suppressions, reproducer and regression.
Controls cover host race/address/UB/leak, device tools, MPI rank logs, systematic schedules, fuzzing, teardown, failures and optimized equivalence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No real sanitizer project, device, automotive or clinical result is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed checker selection, complete builds, coverage ledger, report triage, semantic fixes, suppressions, host/device/MPI boundaries, CI, regression/closure, security and high-stakes limits.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed compiler-driver linking, symbols/build IDs, supported checker shards, positive probes, seeds/target status, first-error artifacts, narrow suppression governance, rank/device logs, resource multipliers, minimization, regressions, production-equivalent tests and protected retention.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter treats tools as conditional evidence, gives exact matrix accounting, counters eighteen misconceptions, supplies ten examples through autonomous braking, and includes five progressive exercises with complete clinical-lab transfer.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner and pedagogical evidence only; no external LLVM/GCC/NVIDIA/USENIX, compiler/runtime/device/MPI/vendor, formal verification, real application, automotive/braking/functional-safety, laboratory-medicine/pathology/clinical-informatics, security/privacy, operations, regulatory/certification, ethics, accessibility/human-factors or independent safety review is claimed. The chapter/model prove neither race freedom, memory safety, tool completeness, application correctness, performance, portability, diagnostic/control validity, privacy, approval nor deployment safety.
